title: Keep facts inside the period asked
statement: Keep every fact in an item, its sample answers and marking notes included, inside the period and region the request names, and check dates in code.
example: In one 1,080-item run, 41 items were found out of period.
detail: Failure analysis of a 1,080-row export of AP history items counted 41 out-of-period items and 39 factual errors, with named anachronism families recurring. Essay marking notes and short-answer sample responses routinely cited years outside the unit, and in a calibration one essay's marking notes used evidence from a region outside the one its prompt named. It holds where a request fixes a period and region, as in the AP history courses.
against: A simple year check caught little on its own: 1 of 7 essay chronology failures, about 14%, with no false positives (icloud-work/aptraining-crystal-copy-20260521/variant-calibration-lab-snapshot/KNOWN_ISSUES.md, lines 135-137).

evidence.quote: **Symptom**: 21 sample_response_error + 41 out_of_period + 39 factual_error + named-content-trap families (`content_lakota_pre1607` 14, `content_muscovy_east_india` 7, `content_navigation_acts` 3, `content_requerimiento_overclaim` 2) = chain hallucinating concrete, name-able anachronisms in Unit 1 content.
**Symptom**: LEQ rubric_notes routinely cite years outside Unit 1 (1491-1607); SAQ sample_responses do the same.
- `apush-u1-1505-leq-medium`: LEQ rubric included Northeastern evidence outside a Southwest / Great Basin prompt.
This creates period drift and can make an item look plausible while testing Unit 2 content. ... later context must be labeled and never required for the Unit 1 key.
Dates matter because they bound what can cause what. ... Context can reach outside a prompt period, but the response must explain the relationship instead of smuggling later knowledge into the claim.
Do not use a later event as period evidence, invent a direct quotation, treat Indigenous societies as interchangeable, or make the stimulus itself reveal the answer.
